title: NeMo-Guardrails breaks Langfuse integration / Runnable config is ignored in LLM call (NVIDIA-NeMo/Guardrails)
raw_text:
NeMo-Guardrails breaks Langfuse integration / Runnable config is ignored in LLM call — open-source issue in NVIDIA-NeMo/Guardrails. Labels: enhancement, good first issue, status: help wanted. When [Langfuse](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/) is used for tracing (instead of Langsmith), the usage of NeMo-Guardrails in a Langchain chain completely breaks the tracing functionality.

The reason seems to be, that the langchain runnable is not called with the runnable config, which defines callbacks for langchain.

summary: This open-source issue highlights a real-world integration challenge between NeMo-Guardrails, Langfuse, and Langchain. title: Cross-vendor byte-identical inference for a 72B LLM (AMD MI300X vs. Nvidia H100)
author: ashsyngh
summary: This news discusses achieving 'byte-identical inference' for a 72 billion parameter large language model (llm) across different hardware vendors, specifically amd's mi300x and nvidia's h100 gpus. title: Meta$^n$: Recursive Self-Improvement through Emergent Depth
author: Zae Myung Kim, Young-Jun Lee, Seungyeon Jwa, Dongyeop Kang
raw_text: Self-improving LLM agents refine answers, not the process that produces those answers. Systems that add a meta-level hold that level fixed, and those that edit themselves must leave part of their own editing machinery untouched to stay stable, capping the meta-depth they realize at roughly two. We present Meta$^n$, which keeps the meta-operation fixed and recurses on its input instead. That operation, $Ω$, is applied repeatedly to its own products, reading the traces of the solver stack below together with the code that produced them, then writing the next layer as a strategic pre-process and a library of callable helpers. Because $Ω$ never changes, it cannot destabilize the system, and because its input strictly grows, each layer reasons from a higher vantage than the last. Depth is set by convergence rather than fixed in advance, and an evolutionary archive searches over layer chains. Across two backbones, Meta$^n$ outperforms prior self-improving agents on all eight benchmark families. The sharpest case is ARC-AGI-2, built to resist skill memorization, where it alone scores above zero. Ablations indicate that most of the gain from recursion comes from the conditioning each layer passes to the next, and distinct layer roles emerge with depth although no prompt prescribes them. Code available at https://github.com/minnesotanlp/meta-n
summary:
this paper, "meta$^n$", explores a novel approach to self-improving llm agents. traditionally, agents might refine their answers or fix a meta-level process. however, these methods often cap the depth of improvement. meta$^n$ proposes a different strategy: it keeps a fixed "meta-operation" and applies it recursively to its *input*, rather than trying to modify its own core editing machinery. by reading the traces of the solver stack below, it achieves deeper, emergent self-improvement. this allows agents to continuously refine their understanding and problem-solving capabilities without becoming unstable.

understanding this concept is important because self-improving agents are a frontier in ai research and development. for roles in aiml and r&d, grasping how agents can autonomously learn and evolve their processes is key to building more sophisticated and capable ai systems. you could read the paper to delve into the mechanics of this recursive self-improvement and compare it to simpler agent architectures you might have studied.
why: explores advanced self-improving llm agents, crucial for building autonomous, capable ai systems.

title: Adapter coverage parity: crash-and-resume verification tests for the LangGraph and OpenAI Agents adapters (Cyrax321/CONTINUUM)
raw_text:
Adapter coverage parity: crash-and-resume verification tests for the LangGraph and OpenAI Agents adapters — open-source issue in Cyrax321/CONTINUUM. Labels: help wanted, adapter. ## Affected component

Adapters (LangGraph, OpenAI Agents, LangChain, generic)

## What problem does this solve?

README's Status section states it directly: the OpenAI Agents SDK and LangGraph adapters do not yet carry the same crash-and-resume verification coverage as the generic facade. That makes it hard to recommend them for production recovery, and it is exactly the kind of gap an external contributor with framework experience can close.

## Proposed solution

Port the crash-and-resume ver
summary: This open-source issue is about adding robust "crash-and-resume" verification tests for the langgraph and openai agents adapters in a project called continuum. essentially, it means ensuring that if an ai agent's process unexpectedly stops, it can pick up exactly where it left off without losing its state or progress. this kind of fault tolerance is critical for any real-world ai application, especially in production environments where reliability is key. the project aims to bring these specific adapters up to the same testing standard as its generic adapter, making them more dependable. for you, understanding this highlights the importance of robust testing and error handling in mlops and software development for ai agents. you could try exploring how state is managed in agent frameworks and how to design tests that simulate failures and verify recovery.
why: Ensures AI agents can reliably recover from failures, crucial for robust MLOps.
